title: Late Breaking Results: Advanced PCB Placement with Irregular Components for Efficient Collision Detection and Routability Optimization
problem: Automated PCB placement must handle heterogeneous components with irregular geometries and complex design rules while ensuring collision-free placement and routability.
motivation: Modern PCBs contain diverse component shapes and constraints; existing placement tools are optimized for regular geometries and struggle with irregular component contours and board boundaries.
method: Three-stage placement framework: (1) global placement with Separating Axis Theorem for collision detection on exact component contours and board shapes, (2) multi-stage force-directed method dynamically adjusting attractive/repulsive forces for clearance and routability, (3) scanline-based legalization resolving overlaps and enforcing spacing constraints. Framework adapts to diverse design limitations.
key_novelty: Separating Axis Theorem-based collision detection for exact irregular component geometries in global PCB placement.
contributions: Global placement with SAT-based collision detection for irregular component contours
Multi-stage force-directed method with dynamic constraint adaptation
Scanline legalization for overlap resolution and spacing enforcement
limitations: Focus on industrial PCB designs; specific performance metrics and quantitative comparisons not fully detailed in abstract.
primary_theme: Collision-aware placement for irregular PCB components
